description: IMS hip mobility targets · structured cue data for PAIL/RAIL prescriptions. The 6 targets cover the primary positions used in the IMS movement system. Default programming favors the first 3 (IR/ER/Extension) · the last 3 (deep flexion / abduction / adduction) only get programmed when explicitly listed as a priority.

targets.name: 90/90 Back Leg · Posterior Capsule (IR Bias)
targets.setup: Sit in 90/90 with the BACK leg bent · ankle and shin on the floor, hip externally rotated. Keep the front leg passive · this is a back-leg drill.
targets.passive_position: Allow the back-leg pelvis to settle · do not force end range. Hands rest forward on the floor for support, spine tall and neutral.
targets.pail_intent: Drive the back ankle and outer shin DOWN into the floor. Imagine you're trying to push the floor away with the entire posterior shin · effort comes from the hip, not the knee.
targets.rail_intent: Try to LIFT the back ankle and shin AWAY from the floor without twisting the trunk or rolling the pelvis. The pelvis stays settled · only the leg moves.
targets.common_compensation: Trunk twist, pelvis lift on the back-leg side, gripping with the foot or knee instead of the hip.
targets.coach_cue: Anchor the back-leg pelvis. Push, then lift, all from the hip joint. Trunk doesn't move.
targets.client_friendly_cue: Press your back ankle into the floor, then try to lift it off without letting your body twist.
targets.contraindication_notes: Recent hip labral repair · check tolerance before loading rotation. Knee meniscus flare · ease into the back-leg knee flexion.

targets.name: 90/90 Front Leg · Anterior Capsule (ER Bias)
targets.setup: Sit in 90/90 with the FRONT leg bent at 90° · shin and ankle on the floor, hip externally rotated. Back leg passive.
targets.passive_position: Hinge slightly forward at the hips over the front leg · spine tall, no rounding through the lumbar. Front-leg hip externally rotated.
targets.pail_intent: Drive the front shin and ankle DOWN into the floor. Pressure comes from the hip · imagine pushing the floor through the side of the shin.
targets.rail_intent: Try to LIFT the front ankle and shin AWAY from the floor without leaning, rotating, or shifting weight back. The pelvis stays square.
targets.common_compensation: Pelvis tilts back, weight shifts off the front leg, lumbar rounds, knee gripping instead of hip.
targets.coach_cue: Stack tall over the front hip. Push the floor, then lift the leg, no shifting back.
targets.client_friendly_cue: Press your front shin into the floor, then try to lift it without falling back or twisting.
targets.contraindication_notes: Anterior hip impingement · stay short of pinch. FAI symptoms · regress the depth before loading.

targets.name: Hip Extension · Couch Stretch Position
targets.setup: Half-kneeling against a wall or couch · back foot elevated, front foot flat, knees stacked vertically. Pelvis tucked posteriorly to lock out the spine and isolate the hip.
targets.passive_position: Hold a tall, posteriorly-tilted pelvis. Allow the hip flexor and quad to lengthen passively without arching the low back. Glute of the back leg stays gently active to support pelvis position.
targets.pail_intent: Drive the back KNEE down and slightly FORWARD as if trying to pull the thigh into flexion. Effort comes from the hip flexor side · low back stays locked.
targets.rail_intent: Squeeze the back-leg glute and try to pull the thigh FARTHER into extension without arching the low back. The pelvis stays tucked.
targets.common_compensation: Lumbar extension (arching), pelvis tipping forward, losing tall spine, quad-gripping instead of hip extension.
targets.coach_cue: Tuck the pelvis. Lock the spine. Then push, then squeeze · all hip, no back.
targets.client_friendly_cue: Pretend someone's pulling the bottom of your ribs toward your hips. Now press the back knee down and forward, then squeeze your butt to drive it back.
targets.contraindication_notes: Knee pain in the down-leg · pad the knee or regress to standing. Acute lumbar flare · skip until calm.

targets.name: Hip Deep Flexion · Loaded Bottom Position
targets.setup: Supported deep squat or seated knee-to-chest with hands on the knee or block. Spine stays as long as possible · don't dump into a rounded position.
targets.passive_position: Allow the hip to flex into the available range · use hands or block for support if the bottom position is unsupported. Breathe into the back of the ribs.
targets.pail_intent: Drive the THIGH or KNEE DOWN into the hands or block as if trying to push the leg back into hip extension. Effort comes from the glute.
targets.rail_intent: Pull the knee CLOSER to the chest using the hip flexors · do not aggressively round the lumbar to gain range.
targets.common_compensation: Lumbar rounding to fake range, ribcage flaring, holding breath, hands pulling instead of hip flexors working.
targets.coach_cue: Long spine. Push the knee down, then pull it up · all hip, no spine.
targets.client_friendly_cue: Push your knee into your hands first, then pull it toward your chest with your hip · keep your back long.
targets.contraindication_notes: Acute meniscus flare · stay shallow. Femoroacetabular impingement (anterior pinch) · stay just short of pinch. Hip replacement · check surgeon's depth restrictions.

targets.name: Hip Abduction · Side-Lying Capsule
targets.setup: Side-lying with the working leg up, knee straight or slightly bent. Lower hip stacked on the floor · keep the trunk square (no rolling backward).
targets.passive_position: Working leg lifted into available abduction range · short of where the trunk wants to compensate.
targets.pail_intent: Drive the working leg DOWN and IN as if trying to adduct it back to the floor. Effort comes from the inner thigh and adductors.
targets.rail_intent: Pull the working leg FARTHER OUT into abduction using the outer hip and glute med · no trunk lean to gain range.
targets.common_compensation: Trunk rolling back, hip hiking, leg drifting forward into hip flexion instead of pure abduction.
targets.coach_cue: Stack the trunk. Push down then lift up, all from the side hip.
targets.client_friendly_cue: Press your top leg down toward the floor first, then lift it as high as you can without rolling backward.
targets.contraindication_notes: Lateral hip pain or bursitis · regress depth and dose. Recent IT band release · check tolerance.

targets.name: Hip Adduction · Side-Lying or Cossack
targets.setup: Side-lying with the bottom leg straight and active OR Cossack squat position with the extended leg's hip adducting. Trunk square.
targets.passive_position: Working leg in adduction · for side-lying the bottom leg lifts toward the ceiling · for Cossack the extended leg straightens with hip adducting.
targets.pail_intent: Drive the working leg OUT (away from midline) as if trying to abduct. Effort from the outer hip and glute med.
targets.rail_intent: Pull the leg INWARD or ACROSS the midline using the adductors · no trunk shifting to fake range.
targets.common_compensation: Trunk shifts toward the working leg, lumbar lateral flexion, gripping with the abs instead of using the adductors.
targets.coach_cue: Trunk stays square. Push out, then pull in · all from the inner thigh.
targets.client_friendly_cue: Press your leg outward like you're pushing it away · then pull it back across using the inside of your thigh.
targets.contraindication_notes: Acute groin/adductor strain · skip until pain-free. Pubic symphysis pain · regress dose.

level_1.label: Foundation · learning the position
level_1.description: Light contractions. Focus on finding the right muscles · don't grind.

level_2.label: Build · tolerated and consistent
level_2.description: Moderate effort. The position is familiar · push enough to feel work, not enough to lose form.

level_3.label: Capacity · advanced, supervised
level_3.description: High effort. Reserve for clients who own the pattern at lower levels and have coach supervision.

level_advanced_supervised.label: Maximum · coach-only
level_advanced_supervised.description: Maximum effort contractions. NEVER printed in client-facing PDFs · coach-supervised only.

default_programming_rules.rule: Default to 1-2 primary targets + 1 supporting target per session. Only program a supporting target if it appears explicitly in the FRA priorities OR the coach selected an advanced hip focus. Six separate hip drills is too much for a normal client plan.
